subject: SCIENCE
title: What Living Things Need
introduction: A plant needs light and water, and a dog needs food and water. Do all living things need the same things?

vocabulary.definition: A living thing that grows in soil and makes food.
Energy that lets us see things.
The liquid all living things need.

activities.instruction: Watch and listen — Milo shows what living things need.

items.prompt: Which statement about living things' needs is true?

options.text: All organisms need shelter in same form
Living things need resources, but not in identical ways. Plants make sugars and need light, water, gases, and nutrients; animals obtain food.

items.explanation: Every living thing needs resources, but needs differ — plants make their own food with light, and animals eat food. Plants do not eat soil.

items.prompt: Which pair matches an organism to what it needs?
items.explanation: A plant needs light and water to make its food. Darkness and sand do not help a plant, and animals need food and water too.
Plants make their own food using light — they do not eat soil. Plants need light and water, and animals need food and water.

options.text: Plants make sugars using light energy.

items.explanation: Plants use light energy to make sugars, which is their food. Animals do not make food from sunlight, and plants do not eat soil.

items.prompt: Which statement about needs is true?

options.text: Plants and animals both need suitable space.
All living things need exactly the same conditions.

items.explanation: Plants and animals both need a suitable space to live in. Needs differ between living things, and plants make their own food.
